description: The pie chart, titled “Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse,” visually represents the proportional distribution of media outlets referenced or analyzed in the study, with each slice corresponding to a specific outlet and its associated percentage. The largest segment, colored dark blue, represents Breitbart at 14%, followed by “Other” at 13% in gray. Drudge Report and The Daily Caller each account for 8%, shown in orange and green respectively. NPR and Vox each hold 6%, depicted in purple and brown. The Guardian and BBC each represent 5%, in pink and dark gray. RT, Daily Kos, National Review, Daily Mail, Red State, Fox News, and CNN each occupy 3%, shown in varying shades of teal, green, red, and purple. Shareblue and PoliticusUSA are also included at 3% each. The chart uses distinct colors for each outlet and includes percentage labels directly on the slices, with no legend provided. The segments are arranged in descending order clockwise from the top, with “Other” placed prominently after Breitbart, suggesting a focus on major outlets while acknowledging a significant residual category. The visual design emphasizes the dominance of Breitbart and the collective weight of smaller or less frequently cited sources under “Other.”
